- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.3) or shows strong bearish momentum, model often overshoots early; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent peak.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model frequently overcorrects; apply a “mean reversion” penalty: subtract 0.5–1.5% of spike magnitude from next forecast.  
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.3–0.7), model often fails to capture mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with 3–5-day moving average of history.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply a “lag correction” by reducing first 5 forecasts by 1–2% relative to true trend.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +1.0 → -0.3 → +0.6), model misreads momentum; reduce forecast volatility by 20–30% in subsequent periods.
